name: Arctic Open
stakes: This Super 500 event offers India's top shuttlers a vital opportunity to gain crucial ranking points and build momentum in the lead-up to the season's major tournaments.
summary: India's badminton contingent arrives in Vantaa for the Arctic Open, a Super 500 event that promises crucial ranking points and a chance to build momentum. Leading the charge are the top-seeded men's doubles pair, Satwiksairaj Rankireddy and Chirag Shetty, who are fresh from their Asian Games men's team bronze. They'll be eager to assert their dominance and continue their impressive run.In the singles categories, PV Sindhu (WR 10) and Lakshya Sen (WR 14) are key figures. Sindhu is navigating the tournament battling fatigue after a gruelling Asian Games campaign, while Sen is actively seeking to regain his peak form following an early exit in Hangzhou. HS Prannoy (WR 24), a vital member of the Asian Games bronze-winning team, will also be aiming for a strong individual showing. The doubles contingent includes Treesa Jolly and Gayatri Gopichand (WR 20), Asian Games quarterfinalists looking to climb higher, and the mixed doubles pair of Dhruv Kapila and Tanisha Crasto (WR 18), focused on building consistency. Promising young talents like Ayush Shetty (WR 20) in men's singles and Malvika Bansod (WR 31) in women's singles are also part of the squad, gaining valuable Super 500 exposure against a competitive international field. The draw for the main rounds is still pending, with all Indian shuttlers awaiting their first-round opponents.
